News.title: Cops appeal for dashcam footage after girl, 17, dead & two other teens injured after car smashes into tree
News.content:
CRASH TRAGEDY Cops appeal for dashcam footage after girl, 17, dead & two other teens injured after car smashes into tree

COPS are appealing for dashcam footage after a teenage girl was killed after a car smashed into a tree leaving two others injured.

Emergency services scrambled to the scene last night but the 17-year-old was sadly found dead.



The teen was driving a blue Seat Ibiza Xcellence between Headcorn and Staplehurst in Kent when it veered off the road at a junction and collided with a tree.

Cops as well as paramedics and Kent Fire and Rescue Service rushed to the scene but the teenage driver was pronounced dead on arrival.



Her next of kin have been informed.

Cops said the two passengers were also injured in the horror smash.

A 19 year old man was raced to a London hospital in a life-threatening condition and a 17 year old boy was taken to a local hospital with serious injuries.

Kent Police is now appealing for witnesses, CCTV and dashcam footage following the fatal collision.

The force is urging anyone who may have witnessed the incident or saw the vehicle beforehand to get in touch.

More to follow… For the latest news on this story keep checking back at The Sun Online

News.title: Bodies of 29 unborn babies found buried at home in Poland by horrified construction workers as woman, 57, arrested
News.content:
BODIES of up to 30 unborn babies were unearthed in a horror discovery at a family home – as a 57-year-old pathologist was dramatically arrested over the grisly find.

Magdalena H. was detained in Zamość on June 12 after prosecutors launched a bombshell probe into the shocking find in Lutoryż, east of Krakow, Poland.





The gruesome discovery was made when construction workers were digging up a driveway on a private plot.

The unborn babies were uncovered by the excavator – sparking panic and an immediate emergency response.

Prosecutors revealed they were first alerted on June 10 after chilling reports of medical waste – including “paraffin blocks and microscope slides” – being discovered on the property.

They said: “Among the discovered debris was a human fetus and other remains that could have been early-stage human fetuses or their fragments.



“Medical experts were dispatched to the scene and confirmed that the recovered remains were those of human fetuses.”

Investigators confirmed the current owners – a young couple – had purchased the plot from a woman working as a pathologist – now at the centre of the probe.

Initial unofficial reports suggested at least 13 tiny remains had been found – but the scale of the discovery quickly escalated.

Later estimates claimed several dozen, possibly as many as 30 fetuses, had been buried beneath the soil, according to Polish media.



Investigators swarmed the site under strict supervision from the prosecutor’s office as the quiet village was plunged into chaos.

Police refused to comment publicly, confirming only that the District Prosecutor’s Office in Rzeszów had taken control of the investigation.

Meanwhile, the once-peaceful neighbourhood was transformed into a full-scale forensic zone.

Police tents, specialist teams in white protective suits and heavy machinery flooded the scene as more remains were uncovered.



Forensic crews wearing masks were seen sifting through the soil around the house, meticulously searching for further evidence.

A table was set up nearby where officers photographed and examined each disturbing discovery piece by piece.

A specialist waterworks truck was also deployed, fuelling fears that drains and sewer systems could hold further evidence.

The excavator used to dig up the soil is being tested for DNA matches as investigators comb through every detail.



A local revealed the property is now occupied by a young couple who unknowingly began the work that exposed the buried secret.

Cops say the investigation is focused on claims a body was tampered with and dangerous waste was dumped illegally.

These offences could land those involved behind bars for up to 12 years.

According to reports, the former owner allegedly admitted during questioning to burying medical waste on the property – as investigators seized medical records and patient files.



Locals described the former resident as unsettling and reclusive.

“I don’t even know what this woman does. I knew her by sight,” one villager said.

Another added the woman, who had red hair, “was a bit strange,” though they could not explain why.

The pathologist is believed to have bought the house two years ago before selling it six months ago to the couple.



Residents said her former practice in Rzeszów is still listed online – but no trace of it now remains.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A man told local media. “I remember that woman, but she hasn’t been here for about five years. She supposedly performed some autopsy here, but I don’t know for sure.”

Investigators are now working on a grim theory – that the doctor buried the fetuses in her garden instead of disposing of them properly, possibly to cut costs.

News.title: Moment postie trips over and breaks fence before miserably failing to fix it
News.content:
THIS is the hilarious moment a postman trips into a flimsy fence and face plants before desperately trying to patch up the damage he caused.

The viral clip, which has more than four million views on X, shows the unlucky postie taking a tumble while delivering mail in the pouring rain.





Though the homeowner who shared the footage demanded answers from Royal Mail, many people reacting to the clip rushed to the defence of the embarrassed worker.

The footage begins with the postman approaching a property as the rain hammers down around him.

He attempts to step over a low wooden barrier separating the pavement from the front garden.

But the move quickly goes wrong.

As he lifts his leg over the obstacle, he appears to misjudge the height and catches his foot.

The postie is then sent sprawling forwards, smashing through the fence before crashing face-first on to the ground.



Two wooden planks snap apart as he lands heavily in the property’s front yard.

The man quickly gets back to his feet and surveys the damage.

He then makes an awkward attempt to repair the fence, lifting one of the broken planks and trying to prop it back into place.

After a brief struggle, he appears to realise the fix isn’t going to work.

The postman eventually abandons the repair job altogether and heads to the front door, where he rings the bell.



The man who posted the footage claimed the mishap happened at his daughter’s property and said he had contacted Royal Mail about repairing the damage.

In a post online, he wrote: “Hey Royal Mail, can you get your postie to bring some tools tomorrow to fix the fence properly.

“It’s there for a reason.”

He claimed the barrier had been installed to stop dogs walking on the grass.

But many social media users were far more critical of the fence than they were of the postman.



One wrote: “Ever heard of an email, why the need to put this on social media.

“What is with people having to humiliate others on social media and bring them down. Pathetic.”

Another said: “It was obviously an accident. Get a hammer and some nails and put the silly bits of wood back together and get over it.”

A third added: “The fella made a tiny, irrelevant mistake, hopping over a fence that literally tempts people to hop over it.

“You can see the look on his face that he felt bad about it. There isn’t a person on the planet who doesn’t take the odd convenient shortcut.”



Another supporter wrote: “The fella made a tiny, irrelevant mistake, hopping over a fence that literally tempts people to hop over it.

“You can see the look on his face that he felt bad about it. There isn’t a person on the planet who doesn’t take the odd convenient shortcut. You will, I do, he did, your family will. It’s normal.

“He clearly isn’t a bad person and clearly didn’t mean any harm. He was obviously going to apologise too based on his body language.”

One user blasted the homeowner, saying: “Could just get a hammer & some nails out take 5 mins to sort that sh*t fence out. Instead you put him is social & risk his job. Top guy you ain’t ya.”

Another wrote: “Flimsy fence in the way, postie slips and breaks it while delivering in the p**sing rain… and you’re shaming him online? Sort it yourself lad, don’t go crying to Royal Mail.”



Others questioned whether the structure qualified as a fence at all.

One said: “That has to be the most annoyingly useless fence I have ever seen.”

Another posted: “It’s not a fence it’s a trip hazard.would remove it before any else sues you. Ps get stop being a keyboard warrior, nobody likes a whiny grass.”

A further commenter raised privacy concerns, writing: “Posting identifiable CCTV footage of a Royal Mail worker publicly on X is not the same as reporting an issue to Royal Mail.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“If there is a complaint, send it privately to Royal Mail. Publicly uploading someone’s image, location and timestamp from domestic CCTV looks like a data protection issue to me.”



The Sun has contacted Royal Mail for comment.

News.title: Mystery as millionaire heiress, 26, is found shot dead at luxury safari lodge – just a day after pal was gunned down
News.content:
SHOOTING RIDDLE Mystery as millionaire heiress, 26, is found shot dead at luxury safari lodge – just a day after pal was gunned down

A MILLIONAIRE heiress has been found shot dead at her family’s luxury South African safari lodge – just one day after a trusted aide was gunned down at the same estate.

Caroline von Rantzau, 26, died from a gunshot wound at the exclusive Leeuwfontein hunting reserve in South Africa’s Limpopo province, where her family are powerful players in the shipping world.





Her death came just one day after financial manager Arno Koën, 44, was found shot dead on the sprawling property – sparking a deepening mystery.

Early claims from the family’s shipping firm suggested von Rantzau, a German shipping heiress, had died in a car crash on June 1.

But police have since confirmed both deaths were caused by firearms.

Koën was discovered on May 31 with a fatal gunshot wound from a 9mm pistol.

Then, just hours later, gunfire shattered the calm of the luxury lodge again.

Witnesses reportedly heard two shots coming from von Rantzau’s private room.

Officers later confirmed she too had been killed by a gunshot wound – believed to have been fired from a .357 calibre hunting rifle.

According to one witness cited by Bild, the weapon came from the gun cabinet of her father, Dr Eberhart von Rantzau.



Detectives from the South African Police Service descended on the estate, spending two days scouring the grounds, gathering evidence and interviewing those inside the tightly controlled reserve.

Despite the intense probe, authorities have yet to explain exactly what unfolded – and no suspects have been identified.

However, no others are currently under investigation.



The double shooting has rocked one of Germany’s most prominent shipping dynasties.

Von Rantzau had been seen as a rising force within the Hamburg-based family empire.

Her father is managing director of Deutsche Afrika-Linien GmbH, which sold its container shipping business to Hapag-Lloyd in 2022.

The family also maintains stakes in container depots across South Africa.

The young heiress had built a life for herself in the country and had recently expanded her footprint, purchasing two more properties near the Mozambique border.



Those close to her said she spent her days caring for animals on the estate and was an enthusiastic hunter.

She was also said to share a close bond with Koën, who handled finances and managed guest bookings at the lodge.

According to Bild, she described him to friends as a kind of “foster father” and “mentor”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police spokesman Malesela Ledwaba said autopsies will now be carried out as investigators work to uncover the truth behind the deaths.

“The results of the autopsy will give investigators information about the actual causes of death and will determine whether investigations will be launched against other persons,” he said.

News.title: ‘Spy turtles and fish’ equipped with sensors are snooping on China’s waters in ‘invisible secret war,’ Beijing says
News.content:
SPY turtles and fish fitted with high-tech sensors have been caught snooping in Chinese waters, Beijing claims.

China has accused foreign powers of using marine life to create “underwater maps” of its coastline as part of an “invisible secret war”.





Beijing‘s Ministry of State Security (MSS) claimed that foreign intelligence agencies are “continuously collecting and stealing sensitive marine data”.

The agency said animals equipped with sophisticated sensors had been discovered gathering information including “water temperature, salinity and ocean currents”.

The MSS also claimed to have recovered surveillance buoys fitted with meteorological and high-precision listening sensors, as well as solar-powered wave gliders.

According to the agency, the devices were capable of capturing real-time port activity and feeding information into a vast “maritime surveillance network”.

The agency warned that such espionage efforts could allow foreign governments to “identify weak points in China’s coastal defences”, posing a serious threat to national security.

Officials have since called for greater scrutiny of equipment received from abroad and urged fishermen to report anything suspicious.



Chinese media reports say the government is even offering rewards of up to £55,000 for uncovering spy devices in the country’s waters.

Military use of marine animals is nothing new.

The US is known to operate a so-called “kamikaze dolphin unit” trained to detect mines, which could prove crucial in keeping the hotly-contested Strait of Hormuz open.

The CIA even has a dedicated section on its website detailing the various animals that have been recruited for espionage missions over the years.

Russia also has allegedly developed a dolphin unit to protect waters around naval facilities in Crimea.



A British intelligence report previously claimed Russia had trained bottlenose dolphins kept in floating harbour pens to “counter enemy divers”.

This latest set of allegations comes amid rising tensions between China and the Philippines in the South China Sea.

Both Beijing and Manila lay claim to many of the same features in the disputed waters.

China has accused the Philippines of “causing trouble” by illegally entering its waters, while Manila has accused Beijing of carrying out illegal maritime research.

Earlier this month, tensions flared when a mysterious vessel appeared near the Scarborough Shoal – one of the most contentious features in the South China Sea.



After more than a week of speculation, Chinese state media identified the vessel as a floating “research facility” operated by the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

The claims also come after the Five Eyes intelligence alliance – comprising the UK, US, Australia, Canada and New Zealand – warned of Chinese agents posing as recruiters.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The operatives allegedly advertised bogus job opportunities in an attempt to obtain sensitive information.

This week, the FBI seized the domains of 13 fake consulting companies accused of posting job adverts targeting current and former US security clearance holders.

News.title: Body of man, 55, found inside empty TGI Friday’s restaurant as murder probe launched & two arrested
News.content:
TRAGIC FIND Body of man, 55, found inside empty TGI Friday’s restaurant as murder probe launched & two arrested

THE BODY of a man has been found inside an empty TGI Friday’s restaurant – as two women are arrested.

Police attended reports of suspicious activity at a derelict building in Sheffield where they discovered the body of a 55-year-old man on Wednesday.





A murder investigation has now been launched with two women, aged 35 and 54, arrested on suspicion of murder on Thursday.

Formal identification is yet to take place but the man’s family has been informed and is being supported by officers.

A scene around the building is expected to remain in place until this evening following the horror discovery.

TGI Fridays has since moved to distance itself from the building, clarifying that the Sheffield Road site was closed in January 2026 and is “no longer owned by the company or any affiliated organisation.”

The Sheffield branch was one of 16 UK restaurants closed after TGI Fridays’ UK operator went into administration.



DCI Laura Procter, Senior Investigating Officer, said: “Officers have been conducting various enquiries since the man’s body was sadly found, with the aim of building up a full picture of the circumstances which led up to this incident.

“I am particularly keen for anyone who may have seen suspicious activity in the area around the TGI Fridays building in the days leading up to Wednesday, to get in touch with us.

“We will continue to work hard to get answers, and this has included arresting two women who remain in custody for questioning.

“If you have any information which you think could help us, no matter how big or small, please come forward.”

Anyone with information is asked to call 101 or report online, quoting incident number 897 of June 10.

News.title: Major swimwear brand issues urgent recall in UK over ‘serious drowning risk’ – warning to ‘destroy item using scissors’
News.content:
FOUR swimwear products have been urgently recalled by a major brand as the product poses a serious risk of drowning.

The retailer has urged users to stop using the product immediately, and destroy the item by cutting it with scissors.





Helly Hansen has urgently recalled four buoyancy aids as manufacturing failures created a serious risk of drowning.

Faults in the jackets meant that they did not provide enough buoyancy and turning momentum to bring someone face up in the water, increasing the risk of water inhalation and potential drowning.

The Office for Product Safety and Standards has ruled that the buoyancy jackets do not meet the requirements of the Personal Protective Equipment (Enforcement) Regulations 2018.

Included in the recall are the Sport II, Comfort Compact, Rider Kayak Vest and Rider Foil Race.



All sizes of the jackets have been flagged – from the Sport II, that has only been recalled in size XXS, meant for 30 to 40kg bodyweight.

Helly Hansen has instructed users to stop using the products with immediate effect, and to destroy all recalled jackets using instructions on its website.

To do this, users must intact the buoyancy jacket by fastening any buckles or zips.

Then, using scissors, the product should be cut across the shoulder seams connecting the front and back panels of the buoyancy aid.



Recalled Helly Hansen buoyancy jackets Sport II – Size XXS (30 to 40kg): Serial numbers: 271011, 271012, 272150, 271612, 275325, 275969, 279873, 281286, 291307

Comfort Compact 50N – All Sizes, All Serial Numbers

Rider Kayak Vest – All Sizes, All Serial Numbers

Rider Foil Race – All Sizes, All Serial Numbers

Once complete, users can send a photograph to Helly Hansen, showing irreversible cuts to the shoulder seams, to receive a refund.

Product users can also contact Helly Hansen to organise a return with the brand itself.

Helly Hansen is a renowned Norwegian outdoor clothing and gear brand, primarily supplying sailing, swimming and snow sports apparel.

The retailer currently has one dedicated UK store based in Cowes, the Isle of Wight, but is widely sold in distributors such as John Lewis, Next and Sports Direct.

News.title: My wife died in the Air India crash… they still not given me her phone back – these questions need to be answered
News.content:
WATCHING horrifying footage of a UK-bound Air India flight smashing into the ground on TV, Mohammed Shoeb Iproliya desperately tried to ring his wife, Nusratjahan Jethara.

For eight long hours after, he continued to call – with each ringing sound pulsating through his veins as he prayed the 28-year-old would pick up. As long as it rang, there was hope she’d survived, he thought. But then came the news dozens of families were dreading: All but one of the 242 on board were dead.



One year on, Mohammed, who lives in Leicester, is one of many grappling with not only the grief of losing a loved one, but the pain of still not knowing exactly why their life was ended so tragically.

For heartbroken relatives like Mohammed, fears of a cover-up have been fuelled by investigators failing to return victims’ phones and claiming they had been destroyed in the disaster – despite ringing.



Just 32 seconds after taking off from Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Airport in Ahmedabad, Air India Flight 171 crashed – killing 241 on board the Boeing 787 Dreamliner, including 53 Brits, and 19 on the ground.

But in the many months that have passed, the crucial question of what caused the disaster remains unanswered.

Families of those killed and whistleblowers have pointed to a series of bombshell evidence, shared with The Sun, that calls into question what investigators have so far claimed.

Why was the tail black box “burnt” despite being at the end of the plane, which was intact? What was really said in the cockpit moments before the crash? And why, 12 months on, have families still not received their relatives’ mobile phones back?

Piecing together why so many people were killed on the London-bound flight is the task of India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), part of the country’s Ministry of Civil Aviation.



So far, the finger of blame has been pointed towards pilot error by Captain Sumeet Sabharwal – sparking major controversy and backlash.

But largely unreported evidence shows a series of massive electrical and systems failures, which whistleblowers say investigators are “ignoring”.

The plane has even been branded an “electrical monster” by Ed Pierson, executive director of US campaign group The Foundation for Aviation Safety [FAS].

Given Boeing’s recent track record of safety scandals, and that Air India has been making a financial loss, experts and bereaved families have noted neither can afford for their reputations to be further tarnished.



The AAIB says, moments after takeoff, the plane reached its peak speed of 180 knots, and immediately after, the pilots shut off the fuel switches.

But physics and aviation engineers have raised doubts over these claims – as if the engines were at full takeoff power, the plane would have kept accelerating after the fuel was cut off, and would reach 184-185 knots.

Because the plane didn’t, it suggests the fuel was cut before reaching peak speed – likely by the plane’s computer, not the pilots.

Aviation Herald’s editor and electronics engineer Simon Hradecky, who lives in London, tells the Sun: “With both engines still at takeoff thrust, the aircraft would accelerate further even if at that very second both fuel switches were selected to CUTOFF and the engines begin to run down.”

Evidence submitted to India’s Supreme Court and Parliament, seen by The Sun, also casts serious doubt on the infamous “cockpit conversation” mentioned in AAIB’s report.



The report has been widely interpreted that Captain Sumeet Sabharwal had manually cut off the fuel.

But in the report, neither fuel nor switches are mentioned.

I surveyed the blackened remains of the Air India crash... this is why the official story doesn't add up BY ROBIN PERRIE, CHIEF FOREIGN CORRESPONDENT A year on from the world’s worst aviation disaster in a decade, the families of the 260 victims are no closer to knowing why the Boeing 737 Dreamliner crashed 33 seconds after take-off. In the aftermath of the tragedy, when I surveyed the blackened remains of the medical college, which had been engulfed in flames after 100 tonnes of jet fuel exploded on impact, the pilot was hailed a hero. Locals I spoke to in a ramshackle apartment block next to the airport, who had witnessed the impact, reckoned he deliberately avoided their homes to avoid greater tragedy. But within weeks, a more disturbing narrative emerged when an interim report strongly suggested the fuel switches had been turned off deliberately, cutting power to the engines. The spotlight turned on Captain Sumeet Sabharwal, 55, a veteran aviator with more than 15,000 hours of flying under his belt. But his furious family hit back, rubbishing suggestions that he had been depressed and would take so many other lives with him in an act of suicide. Another twist emerged earlier this year when pilots on another Dreamliner reported a possible technical fault in their fuel switches. Boeing are still doing tests. A second report is due to be released to mark the anniversary, but it won’t contain a conclusion as to what caused the crash, leaving bereaved relatives such as Miten Patel, 41, still waiting for answers. Miten lost both parents and was horrified to later discover that someone else’s remains had been sent to the UK in the same casket as his mum, Shobhana, 71. He told me this week, ahead of a family gathering today to remember the couple: “There has been a lack of transparency and communication from the Indian authorities all along, and that continues. “Nothing has changed. We’ve not heard from the investigators at all.” After a torturous journey via Abu Dhabi and Mumbai, I arrived in Ahmedabad shortly after, at the same airport which just days earlier had been at the centre of a major operation involving hundreds of police officers, firefighters and paramedics. A short taxi ride took us to the edge of the crash scene, now sealed off and protected by metal fencing. But it could still clearly be seen from the apartment blocks of the poor residential area of Meghaninagar, which is right under the flight path. Geeta Patni, 48, agreed to take us to the roof of her block where the full extent of the devastation caused by the jet could be seen. The top of a tree, almost within touching distance, had been sheared off, showing just how much of a near miss Geeta and her neighbours had had. A nearby garden, lovingly tended for years by local soldiers, was a charred mess. The dozen peacocks and a similar number of dogs which lived there had been burned to death by the fireball that erupted. Nineteen people also died on the ground, mostly in the canteen of the medical college, where they had been having lunch. Geeta was clearly still traumatised by the incident as she told me: “The building was shaking. There was chaos in the street and fire and smoke everywhere. “The plane hit the tree and two more buildings just next to our apartment block. “Any closer and we would have been burnt to death.” The victims’ stories, which began to emerge, were heartbreaking. Khushboo Rajpurohit, 27, was flying to London to start a new life with her doctor husband of just five months. She and Vipul Rajpurohit had not seen each other since shortly after their wedding when he returned to Britain for work. He had been excitedly decorating their house ready for their new life together, and shortly before the flight she had visited her temple one last time to ask for blessings for her journey. Happy Dr Prateek Joshi took a selfie of himself, his wife Dr Komi Vyas, and their three children, on the plane just before take-off as they also headed to the UK to start a new life. It was the last photo of the family ever taken. But among those stories of tragedy emerged the remarkable tale of Vishwash Ramesh, 39, the sole survivor from the plane who walked away virtually unscathed. I caught up with him at his family’s home in the coastal village of Diu, around an hour’s flight from Ahmedabad. His physical injuries were still very visible on his face, but his psychological pain was far greater due to the crushing survivor’s guilt he was struggling with. He had tried to arrange two seats next to each other in row 11 by the emergency exits for him and his brother, Ajay. By the time he came to choose seats, other passengers were sitting in part of the row, so the brothers had to sit separately. He survived the crash in miracle seat 11A, but Ajay was on the other side of the aisle in 11J and died along with the other 240 passengers and crew. Vishwash agreed to pose for pictures on the porch of the house near where women relatives were making chapattis to feed guests after Ajay’s funeral. But, utterly traumatised, he felt unable to speak in great detail about the tragedy and a year later, that has not changed. He released a brief statement ahead of the anniversary in which he said: “I live with significant psychological scars and constant unanswered questions around how and why this happened.” Yet he still feels unable to talk more fully about the tragedy with anyone who calls at his Leicester home beyond his closest family and friends. The families of the victims are also going through a similar ordeal. Miten has drifted into a daily cycle of grieving for his parents, Shobhana, a NHS microbiologist, and financial consultant Ashok, 74, of Orpington, Kent, between 11pm and 3am. During the day and evening, he concentrates on being a busy husband, father and company boss, and it is only in the early hours when his thoughts turn to his beloved parents. He said: “I’m running on about three hours’ sleep every day since this has been going on. “I can’t tell you whether it’s a conscious decision or an unconscious decision to grieve between those hours. “But it has become the norm when I go through old videos, like when they did a speech for my 40th birthday. “Their speech is pure love, and it pushes me to continue through the difficult times. “I think to myself that, one day we all die, and when I do, and I meet them again, I want them to say: ‘Son, we’re proud of you. You didn’t give up. You continued. You did the best you could.’ “ Air India has been accused of a lack of compassion after asking families to complete intrusive questionnaires to assess the amount of compensation each is entitled to. And India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) is also guilty of woeful communication, according to some of the families. As lawyer James Healy-Pratt, aviation partner with Keystone Law, said: “The families want to know how and why their loved ones died. The AAIB have not come close to helping them with that so far.” As today’s anniversary passes, it would be hard enough for Miten and Vishwash to just cope with the pain of losing loved ones. But not knowing why is tearing them apart.

It reads: “In the cockpit voice recording, one of the pilots is heard asking the other why he cut off. The other pilot responded that he did not do so.”

Because the flight computers were failing, experts believe it is highly likely that the pilot was actually asking about the autothrottle or the TO/GA (Takeoff/Go-Around) switch automation disconnecting, not the fuel.

Captain Sabharwal’s elderly father, Pushkaraj, a former employee of India’s Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), has urged the AAIB to properly investigate the plane’s technical history.



“My son is a good pilot. The AAIB report is full of inconsistencies,” the 92-year-old says.

“Why can’t we have an open court of inquiry like India did in earlier crashes?”

Backed by Pushkaraj, the FAS has submitted a dossier of whistleblower information to the US Senate, detailing multiple defects on the crash flight.

Its director, Ed, said the plane has had issues since its maiden flight from Everett, Washington, to Delhi on January 28, 2014. It also had a major fire inside the plane in January 2023.

Several technical anomalies also indicate the plane suffered a catastrophic power failure.



Vishwash Ramesh, the sole survivor of the crash, told how he heard a “loud boom in the back” and saw “green and white lights flickering” in the cabin.

Engineers believe this was a high-voltage inverter exploding in the electronics bay, given the series of failures in the days leading up to the smash.

Vishwash, from Leicester, was not asked by investigators about those claims in the days or weeks after – and was only interviewed eights months after the tragedy.



Pilots from the Federation of Indian Pilots and lawyers argue he should have been interviewed immediately after the crash, when the incident was fresh in his memory.

In the days before the crash, the core data network had degraded, and the fuel tank safety system failed, which likely ultimately made the post-crash fireball worse.

Experts say if the system, which reduced flammability by lowering oxygen levels, had worked there, there may have been more than one survivor.

Meanwhile, satellite data shows the plane was broadcasting multiple power, hydraulic, and flight control faults 15 minutes before takeoff.

Another riddle is the tail black box, which can be seen blackened and burnt in photos from the report.



The AAIB said it was located on the roof next to the end section of the plane, which can be seen nearly intact with no visible fire damage in images published by the bureau.

And yet the forward black box, which saw the full impact of the fire and the massive fireball that erupted from the 54,200 kg of fuel in the plane’s wings, managed to yield 49 hours of data.

Engineers say the heat damage on the tail black box indicates internal electric arcing (short-circuiting), not the post-crash fire.

Lawyer P Joseph, who is among several attorneys demanding an independent investigation, says: “Our petitioners have submitted the plane’s final satellite transmissions, showing serious technical issues with the plane.

“So India’s AAIB should take our evidence and the solo survivor Vishwash’s statement into account before they try to pin it on Captain Sumeet Sabharwal.”



Even if Captain Sumeet had cut the fuel, Joseph questioned: “How can he create a loud boom in the back? How can he deactivate the distress beacon in a 32-second flight? How can he burn the tail black box to a crisp?”

“Why is India’s AAIB not even looking into the possibility of electrical failures on the plane?”

The distress beacon Joseph refers to is mentioned in the AAIB report, where it notes “the emergency transmitter locator (ELT) was not activated”. But it does not give a reason.

Captain Sharath Panicker, a Boeing 787 pilot who has flown 787s in Air India’s fleet, says: “The ELT is engineered to survive the most severe of crashes; activate under a 500 G impact and 260°C fire. So why did it fail to transmit on AI 171?”

Other than the mysteries with the plane’s equipment, whistleblowers have also questioned why the Indian investigating authority is still withholding victims’ mobile phones.



The official reason is to “download any material relevant to the crash”, – but families fear it could be to wipe out data “relevant to the crash.”

Mohammed says he saw news of the crash that morning in the UK and was desperate to reach Nusratjahan.

He tells The Sun how he started calling her mobile, and it kept ringing steadily for the next eight hours.



“I could hear the ring till around 4pm [UK time]; so say until 9.30pm local time in India,” the 32-year-old tells us.

“And then I don’t know if the battery died or rescue officials picked up my wife’s belongings – but I couldn’t reach her mobile after that.”

From his account and phone records, it’s clear his wife Nusratjahan’s phone survived the crash.

But the AAIB is saying otherwise and has not returned the phone to him.

“I miss my wife. As long as that phone kept ringing, I could hope she’d survived,” Mohammed said.



Another person who had such a hope is Sagar Patel.

His mum, Hasumatiben Patel, was in seat 12G in the row behind seat 11A – in which passenger Vishwash Kumar Ramesh sat before his miraculous escape.

Sagar tells The Sun: “That day I was swinging between hope and despair.

“First, I saw the crash – the massive fireball, and my heart sank.

“And then I saw the solo survivor walking out of the inferno.



“A few bruises, but very much alive. I saw his seat number; I thought maybe my mother was trapped in debris.

“She’s a small person; fragile – it will take time, but the rescue officials will get to her.”

But then his worst nightmare was confirmed – no more survivors.

“What brought it home to me was the sight of my two-year-old daughter, she kept wandering around the house, searching and asking for her gran”, Sagar says.

“My mother was the heart of my house; she was adored by all. She is missed so much.”



AAIB “ignoring” the plane’s history and faults on crash day is “criminal”, Air India engineers have said.

They have accused the investigating authority of going after Capt Sumeet instead of the evidence.

Unanswered questions in the cockpit may ultimately only be determined by investigators – but for the families of the 260 people who died, the crash is not an engineering puzzle. It is a daily reality.



A year later, many are still struggling with grief, trauma, financial hardship and the absence of clear answers about what happened to those they loved.

One of those still struggling to rebuild her life is UK-based Zeba, whose mum Mariyam Inayat Padariya, 53, was among those killed.

Mariyam had been travelling to Britain to help care for her two-year-old granddaughter, a long-awaited visit that never happened. I

In the year since the crash, Zeba says she has battled anxiety and depression, eventually leaving her job because there was no one left to help look after her daughter.

“My mum was coming to help with the baby,” she said. “After the crash, everything changed.”



The family says they were not allowed to open Mariyam’s coffin after her body was identified through DNA testing and have received no apology from either Air India or Boeing.

“We want justice,” she syas.

“We can’t get my mum back, but we want the truth about what happened to her.”

The Sun has contacted AAIB, Air India and Boeing for comment.

News.title: 'Reform is using Britain's constitution as a toy to be tossed around whenever they don't get their own way'
News.content:
'Reform is using Britain's constitution as a toy to be tossed around whenever they don't get their own way'

"Reform's Zia Yusuf, who has not been elected to any government position, insists his plans would not provoke division, but threatening constitutional upheaval while dismissing opponents as activists and enemies risks doing precisely that"

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Britain’s constitution is not a toy to be tossed aside whenever politicians fail to get their own way. Yet Reform UK’s Zia Yusuf appears ready to do exactly that.

‌



Speaking in Washington, the spokesperson for home affairs for the party threatened to abolish the House of Lords if it stood in the way of his plans for a Trump-style “deportation force” targeting hundreds of thousands of people.

‌



It is an alarming proposal that should concern anyone who values democratic checks and balances. The idea of importing America’s bitter culture wars, complete with ICE-inspired enforcement squads and conspiracy theories about shadowy foreign funding, is deeply troubling.

‌



Britain’s institutions exist to scrutinise power, not rubber-stamp it. Mr Yusuf, who has not been elected to any government position, insists his plans would not provoke division. But threatening constitutional upheaval while dismissing opponents as activists and enemies risks doing precisely that.

Reform claims it wants to save Britain. Undermining the safeguards that protect our democracy is a strange way of showing it.

$1,000,000,000,000

A trillion dollars.

‌



It is a figure so vast that it is almost impossible to grasp. Yet Elon Musk has now crossed that astonishing threshold, becoming the world’s first $1,000,000,000,000 owner on paper.

His success with SpaceX is undeniably remarkable. Innovation, ambition and risk-taking deserve reward.

But when one individual commands wealth greater than the economic output of most nations on Earth, serious questions must be asked.

‌



At a time when millions struggle with rising bills, housing costs and insecure work, the concentration of such extraordinary wealth highlights a widening gulf between the ultra-rich and everyone else. The issue is not envy. The question is whether economies and tax systems are equipped to deal with fortunes of unprecedented scale.

The trillionaire age demands a serious debate about fairness.

'One of the greatest'

Britain has lost one of its greatest ever artists. David Hockney’s colourful, joyful and instantly recognisable work transformed modern art and brought pleasure to millions around the world.

Article continues below

From Bradford to global acclaim, he never stopped innovating.

His legacy is immense, and his influence will endure for generations.

News.title: 'Charlatan' TV psychic jailed for sexually assaulting two women
News.content:
'Charlatan' TV psychic jailed for sexually assaulting two women

John Starkey, 74, who claimed was an 'internationally renowned clairvoyant' with 40 years of experience, has been jailed for sexually assaulting two women

View Image John Starkey has been jailed

A "charlatan" TV psychic has been jailed for four years and five months after sexually assaulting two women.

‌



John Starkey, 74, claimed he was an "internationally renowned clairvoyant" with 40 years of experience, but his crimes were uncovered after he admitted charges of sexual assault by penetration and two counts of sexual assault.

‌



Sentencing Starkey at Caernarfon Crown Court today, Judge Nicola Jones branded him a "complete charlatan" and slammed his actions as a clear breach of trust.

‌



Starkey, of Rhodfa'r Grug, Upper Colwyn Bay, north Wales, exploited his psychic sessions as a front to carry out the attacks, the court heard.

Police first began investigating him after a woman reported being sexually assaulted by him in Wolverhampton in 2018, reports North Wales Live.

Article continues below

News.title: Judge rejects last-minute bid to block Trump's White House UFC birthday bash
News.content:
Judge rejects last-minute bid to block Trump's White House UFC birthday bash

A judge ruled that the decision to host the upcoming 'UFC Freedom 250' event on the White House lawn did not overstep the Trump administration's authority.

View Image (Image: Getty Images)

A US federal judge refused on Friday to stop the White House from staging a UFC event on the building's South Lawn this weekend to celebrate both the nation's 250th anniversary and Donald Trump's 80th birthday.

‌



District Judge Amit Mehta's ruled against two Virginia residents who filed a lawsuit against the President on June 6, arguing the decision to use the White House lawn as the venue for Sunday's planned UFC mixed martial arts event did not overstep the Trump administration's authority.

‌



Judge Mehta concluded that the plaintiffs likely do not have legal standing to challenge the event and have failed to prove that they would suffer irreparable harm by the event going forward as planned.

‌



The judge also cited the plaintiffs’ “unreasonable delay” in suing to challenge an event that has been in the works for months.

“In the context of an emergency application – and coupled with the fact that the UFC fight date was long ago known – it is fair to say plaintiffs unreasonably delayed bringing suit, undercutting their claims of irreparable harm,” judge Mehta wrote.

Article continues below

News.title: Horror as 29 unborn babies found buried beneath family home
News.content:
Horror as 29 unborn babies found buried beneath family home

Construction workers have discovered the bodies of 29 unborn babies while digging at a family home in Lutory, near Krakow, in Poland - with officers arresting a 52-year-old woman

View Image Police have launched a probe into the horrifying discovery (Image: Getty Images)

The bodies of 29 unborn babies were found by horrified construction workers at a family home in Poland.

‌



The workers were digging through a driveway on private land when they discovered the bodies, which led to the arrest of a 52-year-old woman.

‌



The suspect is now being investigated for desecration of a corpse and illegal disposal of hazardous waste, according to Polish news agency PAP. The offence could result in a jail sentence of between two and 12 years.

‌



According to the prosecutor's office, "a significant amount of medical waste, mainly paraffin blocks and microscope slides," were also found on the property, local media reported.

The current owners of the five acre plot, who were in the middle of renovations, alerted police to the discovery, local reports said.

‌



It sparked a large emergency response, with police still digging the area and searches expected to last until next week.

Polish media outlet Interia Wydarzenia said "according to a statement from the District Prosecutor's Office in Rzeszów, the first information about 'the discovery of significant amounts of medical waste on the premises of one of the properties in Lutory' was received by investigators on June 10."

It added: "The discovered waste also included a human fetus and other remains that could have been human fetuses in the early stages of development or their fragments."

Article continues below

Medical experts were sent to the scene and "confirmed that the secured remains were those of human fetuses," the report said.

News.title: Mum's heartbreaking plea for missing schoolboy, 15, to come home after man arrested for 'murder'
News.content:
Mum's heartbreaking plea for missing schoolboy, 15, to come home after man arrested for 'murder'

Taylor Charlton, who has turned 15 since his disapperance, was last seen on May 8 near a footpath, heading toward a river - his parents issued a heartbreaking plea

View 2 Images Taylor Charlton was last seen on May 8 (Image: Jam Press/@carpster.alex)

A heartbroken mum issued an appeal for her missing 15-year-old son to "come home", as a 20-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder.

Taylor Charlton, 15, was last seen on the night of May 8 and police launched an extensive operation to find the schoolboy, from Barnstaple. Devon and Cornwall Police said an arrest was made at an address in North Devon on Friday after new information was reported to detectives. The cops added that the suspect remains in police custody.

The last confirmed sighting of Taylor, who turned 15 since his disappearance, is on CCTV near a footpath close to Tarka leisure centre in Barnstaple. He was seen heading in the direction of the River Taw.

In a previous public appeal, Taylor's mother, Zoe, said: "Taylor, I am absolutely desperate for you to come home. I love you so much and I am worried sick about you. You are not in trouble. Please reach out to someone. We are all waiting for you with open arms."

His father Alex added: "If there is anything anyone knows, please come forward. Taylor is a loving, loyal and special lad and we can’t wait to have him home again."

View 2 Images Taylor turned 15 since his disappearance (Image: Jam Press/@carpster.alex)

The teenager was last seen wearing a bright blue fitted top, jeans and bright blue Nike shoes. He is about 5ft 8ins tall, of muscular build, with dark brown hair and a moustache.

Detective Inspector Charlotte Heath, who is leading the investigation, said: "Devon and Cornwall Police, supported by specialists from neighbouring forces, have committed extensive resources to finding Taylor over the last five weeks. Sadly, despite this, his whereabouts remain unknown. Much of the information we have gathered does not indicate the involvement of a third party.

"This week, we have received new information that someone may have been involved in harming Taylor and, as a result, we have taken action to fully understand this. That has included the arrest today of a male and his subsequent police interview. Taylor’s family have been informed of this development.

"This remains one line of inquiry, amid many, and we will leave no stone unturned. Our thoughts are very much with his family and friends at this difficult time."

Sector Inspector Andy Wills added: "We remain committed to find answers for Taylor’s loved-ones and fully assessing and acting upon any new intelligence that comes to light as part of this.

"We remain open-minded and all lines of enquiry will be thoroughly reviewed in order to ensure we understand, as far as we are able, what has happened to Taylor. Our officers are working tirelessly to ensure this, and all, relevant lines of enquiry are fully investigated.

Article continues below

"We know how upsetting and concerning this news will be for Taylor’s family, friends, and the wider community. Taylor’s family continue to be updated and supported by specialist officers.

"We are asking members of the public to help us by avoiding speculation, especially sharing any unconfirmed information online, and allowing detectives to continue our investigation."

News.title: Eat these specific everyday fruits to slash your risk of heart disease
News.content:
Eat these specific everyday fruits to slash your risk of heart disease

Eating fruit as part of a healthy balanced diet is important - but some varieties offer far more health benefits than others. So what should you be reaching for in the fruit bowl?

View 20 Images Some fruits are considerably more beneficial than others (Image: Getty Images/fStop)

We all know the importance of eating a healthy diet - and that includes eating plenty of fruit. But which items actually give the best bang for their buck? While hitting your five-a-day is a key part of a rounded diet, a new study reveals that some fruits offer significantly more nutritional value than others.

‌



Health experts recommend consuming at least five portions of a variety of fruit and vegetables every day. According to the NHS, a single adult portion translates to:

‌



Small fruits (2 or more items): 2 plums, 2 satsumas, 2 kiwi fruits, 3 apricots, 7 strawberries, or 14 cherries.

Medium fruits (1 item): 1 apple, 1 banana, 1 pear, 1 orange, or 1 nectarine.

Large fruits (1 slice): Half a grapefruit, a 5cm slice of melon, a large slice of pineapple, or 2 slices of mango.

‌



However, a major study involving scientists from the University of Reading, Harvard Medical School, the University of California Davis, and Mars has confirmed that not all portions are created equal when it comes to heart health. The secret weapon? Flavanols.

View 20 Images Experts advise eating 5 portions of fruit and veg a day (Image: Getty Images/Tetra images RF)

Flavanols are natural compounds, which help neutralise harmful free radicals in the body and are widely recognised for boosting cardiovascular and cognitive health.

‌



The study, which tracked the diets of more than 30,000 participants across the UK and United States, found fewer than one in five people consume enough flavanols to actively reduce their risk of heart disease - even those who regularly hit their five-a-day target.

"Most people assume that eating plenty of fruit and vegetables covers this", said Dr Javier Ottaviani, the paper's lead author. "But what this research shows is that the specific choices you make matter far more than the total amount.

"Including a handful of blackberries, a whole apple or having a cup of green tea alongside your meal could make a real difference to how much of these beneficial compounds you actually consume and absorb from the diet."

‌



So which foods should we be reaching for? The foods with the highest flavanol content per portion are:

Plums (500g, roughly one punnet): approximately 450mg of flavanols Cranberries (250g, roughly one punnet): approximately 300mg of flavanols Blackberries (200g, roughly one punnet): approximately 250mg of flavanols Green tea (one 250ml cup): approximately 200mg of flavanols Broad beans/fava beans (80g, a small handful): approximately 140mg of flavanols Cherries (400g, roughly one punnet): approximately 130mg of flavanols Apples with skin (200g, one medium apple): approximately 110mg of flavanols Strawberries (200g, roughly one punnet): approximately 90mg of flavanols Blueberries (150g, roughly one punnet): approximately 80mg of flavanols Pinto beans (40g, two tablespoons dry): approximately 70mg of flavanols

Professor Gunter Kuhnle of the University of Reading said: "Five-a-day is the right message, but we may need to think more carefully about which five. Different fruits and vegetables offer very different nutritional benefits beyond vitamins and minerals, and as our understanding of these compounds grows, there is a real opportunity to make dietary guidance more specific and more effective. This research is a step towards understanding what that might look like in practice."

‌



Of course, all fruits provide major health benefits and are a key part of a healthy and balanced diet. But, flavanols aside, some have more to offer than others. Let's take a closer look...

Blueberries

When it comes to fruit, blueberries can't be beat. They are jam packed with vitamin C, fibre and antioxidants - especially anthocyanins, a purple pigment that gives the berries their deep colour. The little powerhouses promote heart health, regulate blood sugar, and may enhance brain function and exercise recovery - all while remaining incredibly low in calories.

View 20 Images Blueberries are jam-packed with goodness (Image: Getty Images)

‌



One study has shown that people who ate 200g of blueberries two hours before a test achieved better scores, while another linked 180g of blueberries with better memory, accuracy and concentration.

Of course, blueberries can be expensive so rather than buying fresh, consider frozen. Frozen berries often contain more nutrients because they are typically frozen within hours of being picked. Their fresh counterparts, meanwhile, can take days to arrive in the shops, by which time their nutrients can begin to deplete.

Raspberries

Raspberries are packed with nutrients that can reduce inflammation and prevent chronic diseases. They are packed with vitamin C and potent antioxidants - but their main health benefits stem from their incredibly high fibre content. Fibre is crucial for a healthy digestive system, keeps you feeling full, promotes regular bowel movements, and nourishes healthy gut bacteria.

‌



View 20 Images Raspberries have an incredibly high fibre content (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

The antioxidants, meanwhile, help combat oxidative stress, which is linked to inflammation, ageing and chronic disease, like cancer and heart disease.

Just like blueberries, consider buying frozen - not least because raspberries are highly perishable and can quickly turn mouldy.

‌



Strawberries

A summer staple, strawberries are a nutritional powerhouse that offer a wide array of health benefits. A single 100-gram serving (about 8 medium berries) contains just 33 calories but provides more than your daily recommended intake of vitamin C, which helps with collagen production, and immune defence.

View 20 Images Strawberries offer a wide array of health benefits (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Strawberries are also rich in anthocyanins and polyphenols. These antioxidants help lower "bad" (LDL) cholesterol and regulate blood pressure, reducing your risk of heart disease and strokes. Furthermore, regular consumption of strawberries is associated with better cognitive preservation and a lower risk of age-related brain conditions.

‌



Plums

Plums are highly nutritious, low-calorie fruits that are packed with antioxidants, fibre, vitamins (A, C, and K), and minerals like potassium. They support overall health by aiding digestion, reducing chronic disease risks, and boosting heart and bone health.

View 20 Images Plums have been linked to better bone density and gut health (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Furthermore, consuming plums and prunes is linked to better bone health and density, and are excellent for gut health.

‌



Cranberries

Cranberries are antioxidant-rich superfoods packed with Vitamin C, E, K, and are famous for preventing urinary tract infections (UTIs) by stopping bacteria from adhering to the bladder walls.

View 20 Images Cranberries are packed with Vitamin C, E, K, and polyphenols (Image: Getty Images)

They also support heart health, digestive wellness, and oral hygiene by preventing plaque from forming and lowering the amount of acid in your mouth, which can protect against cavities and gum disease.

‌



Blackberries

Blackberries have a high fibre content compared to many other fruits, which can help prevent common digestive issues like constipation and bloating, and which works as a prebiotic to nourish healthy gut bacteria.

View 20 Images Blackberries promote healthy digestion, reduce inflammation, and regulate blood sugar levels (Image: Getty Images)

They are also loaded with polyphenols, particularly anthocyanins, which give the berries their deep purple colour.

‌



Research has shown that anthocyanins increase blood flow to the brain, and can actively reduce brain inflammation linked to age-related cognitive decline.

Studies suggest this protection helps defend against Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases.

Kiwis

Kiwis are exceptionally rich in vitamin C and E; one single kiwi offers 47mg of vitamin C, surpassing the 40mg recommended daily intake, and offers around 10% of our vitamin E intake.

‌



View 20 Images One kiwi offers a whopping 47mg of vitamin C (Image: Getty Images/EyeEm)

Green kiwis also contain a unique natural enzyme called actinidin that helps break down proteins and supports efficient digestion, and they have a high potassium and low sodium profile, which can help regulate blood pressure.

To get the maximum benefits kiwis have to offer, eat whole - including the skin.

‌



Oranges

One orange provides over 90% of your daily vitamin C, making them an excellent choice for protecting our immune system and skin health. And since they are rich in antioxidants and flavonoids like hesperidin, oranges also help reduce inflammation and can lower cholesterol and blood pressure.

View 20 Images Oranges contain over 90% of your daily vitamin C requirement (Image: Getty Images)

However, oranges are very acidic, which can wear down the enamel on our teeth. “It’s best to consume them as part of a meal,” Nichola Ludlam-Raine, a registered dietitian and the author of How Not to Eat Ultra-Processed, told the Telegraph. For example, eat cheese, vegetables or bread after an orange to reduce the amount of acid in your mouth.

‌



Apples

A perfect on-the-go snack, apples are packed with soluble fibre (pectin), essential antioxidants (like quercetin), and vitamin C. Together, these nutrients help to stabilise blood sugar, lower LDL (bad) cholesterol, and feed healthy gut bacteria to reduce chronic inflammation.

View 20 Images Apples are convenient and contain essential antioxidants (Image: Getty Images)

They also contain vitamin C and various antioxidants which help to sustain a healthy immune system.

‌



Like oranges, they do have a moderately high sugar content, however, and consuming them in large quantities - especially in juice form - can impact blood sugar levels. It's recommended to have a maximum of around 150ml of fresh fruit juice a day.

Instead, try to eat them as part of a snack, perhaps paired with a handful of nuts, to help slow down the release of sugars.

Pears

Pears are highly nutritious, low-calorie fruits loaded with dietary fibre, vitamin C, potassium, and antioxidants. A medium pear (around 102 calories) provides approximately 6 grams of fibre, covering about 20% of your daily needs, and they are high in pectin which feeds healthy gut bacteria.

‌



View 20 Images Pears can help with weight loss (Image: Getty Images)

Pears also contain procyanidins and quercetin, antioxidants that can decrease heart tissue stiffness, reduce inflammation, lower LDL ("bad") cholesterol, and regulate blood pressure.

They can also help with weight loss; being water-dense (about 85% water) and rich in fibre, pears keep you feeling full for longer. They are high in natural sugars, however, so moderation is key.

‌



For maximum nutritional value and fibre intake, it is recommended to eat pears with the skin on.

Peaches

Peaches are full of antioxidants and can help improve heart health, aid digestion, and protect your skin.

View 20 Images Peaches can help improve heart health and aid digestion (Image: Getty Images/Westend61)

‌



They are also loaded with polyphenols and carotenoids, which combat cell-damaging free radicals linked to oxidative stress and diseases like cancer. And research has shown that peaches may help reduce allergy symptoms by preventing the release of histamines.

But, as Ludlam-Raine notes, they are high in sorbitol and fructose, which are short-chain carbohydrates that are poorly absorbed in the small intestine. As a result, they can contribute to bloating and discomfort in sensitive individuals with IBS.

Cherries

Cherries are high in antioxidants and get their rich colour from anthocyanins and polyphenols, which help fight free radicals and reduce oxidative stress linked to chronic diseases like cancer and diabetes.

‌



View 20 Images Cherries can help promote better sleep (Image: Getty Images)

They also promote better sleep since they contain melatonin, tryptophan, and serotonin, which regulate your sleep-wake cycle and aid more restful slumber.

Potassium and fibre help regulate blood pressure, balance fluid levels, and manage cholesterol, and cherries also boast strong anti-inflammatory properties that can help manage joint discomfort and alleviate symptoms of arthritis.

‌



Again, they are high in natural sugar, so it’s important to consume in moderation.

Grapefruit

Half of a medium-sized grapefruit provides a significant portion of your daily vitamin C, and also contains vitamin A, which protects against inflammation and infections.

View 20 Images Grapefruit has long been considered a 'diet food' (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Its potassium content can help lower blood pressure by relaxing blood vessel walls, and since it is also rich in fibre, grapefruit are known to support healthier cholesterol levels.

It's long been considered a diet food; grapefruit is high in water and fibre, which helps promote a feeling of fullness and therefore can reduce your overall calorie intake.

However, you must avoid grapefruit - and their juices - while taking certain statins. They contain compounds that block the liver enzyme CYP3A4, which is responsible for breaking down certain statins. When consumed, your body absorbs a much higher dose of the medication than intended, increasing your risk of liver damage and severe muscle pain, according to Harvard Health. It doesn't affect all statins, so it's important to review your specific medication and diet with your doctor or pharmacist.

‌



Mangoes

Mangoes help support a healthy immune system, improve skin and hair health, and aid digestion. They are packed with vitamins A, C, and E, potassium, and antioxidants, and also improve eye health, since they are rich in beta-carotene, lutein, and zeaxanthin, which help protect the retina, reduce glare discomfort, and support overall vision.

View 20 Images Mangoes can help improve your eye health (Image: Getty Images/500px)

While incredibly healthy, mangoes are naturally very sweet and contain more sugar than many other fruits. Portion control is therefore key, especially for those with diabetes.

‌



Grapes

Quick and easy to eat on the go, grapes are a highly nutritious, antioxidant-rich snack that support heart health, digestion, and hydration.

The red and purple varieties, in particular, contain powerful antioxidants like resveratrol, which helps reduce inflammation and supports cardiovascular health, and they are also an excellent source of vitamins K and C, as well as potassium and fibre.

View 20 Images Grapes are an excellent source of vitamins K and C, as well as potassium and fibre (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

‌



However, they are high in natural sugars and calories, which can lead to blood sugar spikes or weight gain if overeaten. A standard 1-cup serving (about 150 grams) contains roughly 15 to 23 grams of sugar.

Whole grapes can also pose a serious choking hazard for young children.

Bananas

A banana is a highly nutritious, convenient fruit that is packed full of potassium, fibre, and vitamins. A medium banana provides roughly 10% of your daily needs for potassium and vitamin C, alongside heart-healthy fibre. And they are a brilliant fat-free source of quickly digestible carbohydrates, making them ideal for pre- or post-workout energy.

‌



View 20 Images Bananas are highly nutritious and ideal for pre or post-exercise (Image: Getty Images)

But compared to other fruits (like berries or melons), bananas are higher in calories and natural sugars, which can lead to weight gain if eaten in excess. Overripe bananas can contain even more, as the starch in the fruit is converted to sugar as they brown.

Pineapple

Pineapple is packed with essential vitamins, antioxidants, and bromelain - a unique digestive enzyme that has anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties and which helps break down proteins and ease bloating.

‌



View 20 Images Pineapples are rich in antioxidants (Image: Getty Images)

One cup provides a large portion of your daily recommended intake of vitamin C (for immunity) and manganese (for bone health) and it is antioxidant-rich to help protect your cells against oxidative stress and chronic disease.

However, because they are highly acidic, pineapples can trigger heartburn or acid reflux, while the blood-thinning effects of bromelain may increase the risk of bleeding for those already taking blood-thinning medications. They are also high in natural sugars, around 8g per serving.

‌



Melon

Melons are composed of about 90% water, making them highly effective for quenching thirst and providing excellent hydration. They contain essential vitamins like Vitamin C for immune support, Vitamin A for eye health, and powerful antioxidants like lycopene, while nutrients like potassium and citrulline can help relax blood vessels, regulate blood pressure, and improve cholesterol levels.

View 20 Images Melons contain essential vitamins like Vitamin C for immune support, and Vitamin A for eye health (Image: Getty Images)

But they are low in fibre compared to other fruits, and they also contain a moderate amount of natural sugar, with 5.7g per serving.

Article continues below

People with compromised kidney function should monitor their intake, as the high potassium content in certain melons can overtax the kidneys.

News.title: Daughter's tragic update after dad 'drugged and bashed to death with a baseball bat by his own family'
News.content:
Daughter's tragic update after dad 'drugged and bashed to death with a baseball bat by his own family'

A dad vanished two weeks ago while on a trip to India - and police now allege he was murdered by his brother and his remains were thrown into a canal

View 4 Images Sunil Sharma vanished while on a trip to India (Image: 7NewsMelbourne)

The daughter of a teacher who was allegedly drugged and beaten to death has released a tragic update just days after four of her family members were charged.

Sunil Sharma, from Melbourne, Australia, vanished while on a visit to India last month to oversee renovations on investment properties. The maths teacher went missing on May 22 while in Amritsar, in the Punjab state, but Indian police now believe the 66-year-old was potentially murdered by his own brother over a property dispute.

Four people have been arrested as part of the investigation, despite police not yet recovering the Australian man's remains.

View 4 Images Sunil Sharma was a father-of-two (Image: 7NewsMelbourne)

Indian police have claimed that Sunil's brother, Satish Sharma, spiked his brother's drink will sleeping pills then fatally bashed him in the head with a baseball bat.

Cops have also alleged that the Melbourne teacher's body was dumped in a canal, as the search for his remains continues. The brother was arrested and charged with murder, along with Sunil's sister-in-law and nephew who were also charged with an alleged cover-up.

View 4 Images His daughter Surbhi shared a heartbreaking message (Image: 7NewsMelbourne)

Days after they were arrested, Sunil's daughter shared an emotional post on social media, saying: "I want to say clearly: do not associate my dad with the actions of his 'brother'. My dad supported his brother and his family financially and emotionally throughout his whole life and raised him like a son.

"Dad was a good man and a victim of an unthinkable betrayal that still cannot be comprehended by our own family. A part of us has been lost to a heinous crime that should never have happened. I pray that the justice system in India enforces the maximum penalty for everyone involved in this calculated and premeditated crime. My dad deserves nothing less."

The heartbroken daughter added that she has received support from the school her father worked at and thanked them. She said: "There is real comfort in knowing that his soul would be at peace seeing just how deeply loved and respected he is by this community.

View 4 Images Police is India alleged Sunil was killed by his brother over a property dispute (Image: 7NewsMelbourne)

"To everyone who commented about my dad as a maths teacher, he would have loved to see that. It means everything to know he gave the gift of education and shaped the lives of hundreds of students."

Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) in Amritsar, Kanwalpreet Singh, claimed the brother killed Sunil "out of greed" and to commit fraud. He told a press conference: "When they took the victim from his house, they gave him sleeping pills. After administering the pills, they struck him on the head with a baseball bat, causing a head injury and killing him.

"Afterwards, his son was present there and his wife also came. They tried to get rid of evidence. Satish Sharma, out of greed for money, prepared a forged power of attorney. Using that power of attorney, they made deals to sell a house."

A fourth person, a property dealer, was also arrested and local police said they are looking for two other people believed to be involved in the death.

Article continues below

A spokesperson at Victoria's education department and the school were the dad worked shared a touching message, saying: "Mr Sharma was a dedicated and valued member of the Diamond Valley college community. News.title: Keir Starmer will fight leadership challenge as he admits he must 'turn things around'
News.content:
Keir Starmer will fight leadership challenge as he admits he must 'turn things around'

After his Government was rocked by the resignation of Defence Secretary John Healey, Keir Starmer argued he’d made 'hard-edged choices' to fund military spending

View 2 Images Keir Starmer acknowledged he needed to turn things around after a series of crises

Keir Starmer has insisted he would fight any leadership challenge - but acknowledged he needed to “turn things around”.

‌



After his Government was rocked by the resignation of Defence Secretary John Healey, the Prime Minister argued he’d made “hard-edged choices" to fund the long-delayed Defence Investment Plan (Dip) by asking all departments to cough up.

‌



And he issued a veiled warning to his rivals, saying any would-be successor would face the same challenges to balance the books while keeping Britain safe. “I would just gently say this: that whoever is Prime Minister is going to face the same prevailing winds as I am facing," he said.

‌



The PM was dealt a significant blow by the shock resignation of Mr Healey, after bitter internal rows over how to fund military equipment and infrastructure over the next decade. He accused Mr Starmer of putting the nation's safety at risk, saying he was “unable, and the Treasury has been unwilling” to stump up enough cash to fund the Dip.

Mr Healey was followed out the door by Al Carns, the Armed Forces Minister, and two ministerial aides.

Dan Jarvis appointed Defence Secretary hours after John Healey's shock resignation READ MORE :

Were John Healey and Al Carns right to resign over military spending? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

View 2 Images Defence Secretary John Healey quit on Thursday with a blast at Keir Starmer's military spending plans (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The crisis comes at a moment of peril for Mr Starmer, only days away from the Makerfield by-election which could see his arch-rival Andy Burnham return to Parliament. Former Health Secretary Wes Streeting also has his eyes on the top job - but has said he would wait until after the by-election to mount a challenge.

But Mr Starmer told the BBC: “I’m not going to go away. I don’t think we should plunge the country into the chaos of a leadership election.”

He added: “I don’t think it should happen, but if it does then I will fight. And let me just be clear... That’s not about personal vanity, it’s not about stubbornness. It’s out of a very deep sense of duty.

‌



"I was elected to serve this country. Notwithstanding the difficult circumstances, that is what I am doing. And in the last few weeks, others have made their own case. I’ve been concentrating on the job I was elected to do, which is to deliver for this country.”

Asked if he would lead Labour into the next general election, expected in 2029, he said: “Well, that’s what I want to do. I recognise that I’ve got to turn things around. We had a very bad set of elections.”

The explosive row over the funding of the defence plan has cast doubt over its credibility, as the £13.5billion proposed by Government falls well below demands from military chiefs. Defence sources said the offer amounted to only £10billion of extra cash, and said the remainder was "Treasury trickery".

Article continues below

But the PM said he had overseen “the biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the 1980s” and every government department had submitted cuts to non-frontline spending to help finance the Dip. "These are hard edged decisions," he said. “Decisions in government involve trade-offs, so they always have to come with that second question: ‘Well, if you’re going to do that, what is it you wouldn’t do?’”

Downing Street said the Dip was still being finalised as new Defence Secretary Dan Jarvis and Chief of the Defence Staff, Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton, met the PM for talks on Friday.

The plan was originally due to published in autumn 2025 but the internal rows kicked the timeline back. Mr Starmer has now set a new deadline of July’s Nato summit.

News.title: Former Arsenal midfielder Thomas Partey denied entry to Canada for Ghana's World Cup opener
News.content:
Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey will miss his nation's first World Cup game in Toronto against Panama, after being denied entry to Canada.

Partey, 32, has pleaded not guilty to seven charges of rape and one count of sexual assault relating to allegations by four different women between 2020 and 2022.

He is due to stand trial next year.

In a statement, Fifa confirmed the former Arsenal player, who is now with Spanish side Villarreal, will be unable to travel from Ghana's training base in Boston, where he is currently located after having his "visa application refused by the Canadian government".

World football's governing body, added: "Fifa is not involved in the immigration processes of host countries, including the adjudication of visas.

"The host government ultimately determines who receives a visa and is admitted into the country."

On the Canadian government website, rules around visiting the country state: "If you have committed or been convicted of a crime, you may not be allowed into Canada."

Partey has pleaded not guilty to all charges and has not been convicted, but is awaiting trial.

A US Customs and Border Protection official added: "The US is aware of the pending court case for Mr Partey, however, at this time, he has not been convicted of a crime and was admitted to the United States after being issued a visa.

"Admissibility determinations are made on a case-by-case basis using law enforcement, national security, and immigration information available at the time of inspection.

"CBP [customs and border protection] officers have the authority to question travelers, conduct inspections, and determine admissibility consistent with US law. CBP defers to Canada for questions on his denial of entry. "

BBC Sport has approached the Ghana Football Association and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) for comment.

News.title: Watch: Four UFO videos newly declassified by US government
News.content:
The Pentagon has released four eyewitness videos as part of its drive to declassify documents related to unidentified flying objects (UFOs).

The clips, which were sent to the FBI, show bright orbs moving in the sky. The government says they were all filmed in the same general area of the northeastern US, but it does not say precisely where this was.

They were recorded between 2021 and 2025 and correspond with other eyewitness reports from the region, the US Department of Defense says.

This is the US government's third release of UFO-related videos and documents. It says the materials originate from "unresolved cases", meaning the government is "unable to make a definitive determination on the nature of the observed phenomena".
